full.description: This is a gross pathology photograph of a bowel specimen, specifically showing a segment of the intestine surrounded by inflamed mesenteric fat. The tissue displays significant thickening, fibrosis, and dark discoloration characteristic of transmural inflammation. These macroscopic features are typical of regional enteritis, also known as Crohn's disease, affecting the bowel wall and mesentery.

random.description: This is a gross pathology photograph showing a segment of the gastrointestinal tract, likely the intestine or mesentery, surrounded by adipose tissue. A wooden toothpick or similar foreign body is seen penetrating the tissue, causing localized inflammation, hemorrhage, and perforation. The visual findings are consistent with bowel perforation caused by an ingested foreign body, such as a toothpick.
